description: We are a small team of AI engineers working on the Flame in Freefall challenge, using AI and data analysis to draw fire-safety insights from NASA microgravity combustion data.
summary: FlameLedger summarises and ranks 21 NASA combustion investigations (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, SAME, ACME, FM2 and more) for five habitat types: crew spacecraft, space station, lunar base, pressurized rover and Mars base. It also keeps a hand-verified evidence ledger of 15 materials. Materials are screened for flammability on Earth, but flames behave differently in microgravity and partial gravity. For example, a PMMA rod spread steadily at 13.6% O2 on the ISS (BASS-II wind-tunnel flow, not cabin ventilation) against a 16% O2 1g blowoff limit, a published margin of −2.4% O2. FlameLedger collects the published NASA results material by material, links every number to its NASA source page, and shows where the evidence runs out: of 15 materials, 14 have Earth-gravity results but only 5 have microgravity evidence, and 49 of 75 material-by-environment cells are empty. Its Habitat Review agent gives each material a deterministic verdict for one or several habitat atmospheres, and the Ask page answers plain-English questions. In both, Gemini writes the text and a verifier checks every AI number and citation against the NASA sources before anything is shown. The project supports NASA's FM2 lunar experiment with three hypotheses registered before it flies.
details: What it does. FlameLedger has five pages and an open API. 1. Evidence Ledger: computed metrics, a coverage grid of materials x environments (1g, ISS microgravity, lunar, Mars, FM2) and all published oxygen margins, ranked. Each cell opens the underlying values with the NASA document, page or table, and a short quote. 2. Habitat Review (AI agent): the user picks a habitat preset (e.g. lunar habitat 34% O2 / 8.2 psia, from NASA's FM2 presentation) or enters custom values, and lists materials. Deterministic rules assign red (burned in reduced gravity at or below this O2), orange (thin or negative published margin), green (self-extinguished at this gravity level at or above this O2) or white (no comparable space data: test needed). Every applicable verdict is listed, with caveats on pressure, test-duct flow vs. cabin ventilation, and partial gravity. Gemini then explains the verdicts; a verifier checks that every cited source was in the evidence given, that every number matches it within +/-0.1, and that no number appears in the prose without a claim. If verification fails twice, only the deterministic table is shown. Users can download the full report as a PDF. 3. Investigations: 21 NASA combustion investigations (BASS, Saffire, SoFIE, FLARE, FM2, LUCI, FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI, the six ACME experiments, SPICE, SLICE, SAME, SAME-R, DAFT, water mist), each summarised with objective, fuels and sample sizes, conditions, variables, measurements and hardware. They are ranked by relevance to a crew spacecraft, space station, lunar base, pressurized rover or Mars base, with the reason behind every score, and can be filtered by prevention, detection and suppression and compared side by side. Includes fire safety on Earth and a data guide for modellers. 4. Ask: plain-English questions answered by Gemini from the catalogue and ledger only; the answer is shown only after the verifier checks every number and citation, and the sourced evidence is always listed. 5. Partial gravity & FM2: NASA drop-tower data show the lunar-gravity limit below both the 0g and 1g limits for all three materials tested, so, for those materials and under drop-tower criteria, 0g and 1g did not bracket lunar gravity. The page shows FM2's four planned tests and three pre-registered qualitative hypotheses, each with a refutation criterion. Benefits. Habitat and materials engineers, researchers and students can see in seconds which materials have reduced-gravity evidence for their atmosphere, and which tests are missing. The verified ledger is reusable through a JSON/CSV API. How we built it. FastAPI and pydantic serve a static HTML/CSS/JS frontend with hand-built SVG charts (no CDN, strict Content-Security-Policy). The data lives in CSV files that are validated at startup; unverified rows never reach the API. There are 167 automated tests. It is deployed on Render. Live app: https://flameledger.onrender.com Use of AI. In the product, Google Gemini writes plain-language explanations of verdicts on the Habitat Review page and answers questions on the Ask page; it does not decide verdicts, and its output is shown only after the verifier confirms every number and source against the NASA evidence. In development, an AI coding assistant helped write code and documentation; the team reviewed all of it. No data is AI-generated: every ledger value was checked by a human against the NASA PDF. Limitations. The ledger is small and hand-verified. Lunar and Mars values come from short drop-tower tests. Only published margins are shown, and there are no numeric lunar or Mars predictions. This is research decision support, not certification. Not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA. Uses public NASA data.
